stories.headline: Anduril explores Israel operations, courting Elbit and DDR&D candidates for local manager

key_facts.fact: Anduril is exploring an Israeli expansion and in talks to recruit a local manager to build ties with Israeli startups and identify partnership opportunities, Calcalist reported.
Meetings in recent weeks were held with potential candidates from Elbit Systems and the Directorate of Defense Research and Development (DDR&D) at Israel's Ministry of Defense.
Anduril is also weighing setting up a local R&D operation and hiring Israeli employees; the local arm would handle sales to the Israeli Ministry of Defense and R&D for global products.

Founder Palmer Luckey — who has described himself as a 'radical Zionist' — visited Israel in February on a trip organized by Lux Capital's Josh Wolfe that included a meeting with PM Benjamin Netanyahu.
Anduril has already signed agreements with several Israeli startups, including ASIO, which is expected to supply components for Anduril's unmanned aerial systems.

stories.headline: China hits 10 US firms with export controls and bars 46 from procurement in retaliation for Pentagon list

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US entities to its export control list on Monday, prohibiting exports of dual-use items to them effective immediately.
The 10 firms include Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace & Technologies, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
China's Finance Ministry separately barred government entities from buying products from 46 US companies, including multiple units of Lockheed Martin, Raytheon and General Dynamics.

Beijing framed the move as retaliation for the US Defense Department's expansion of the Section 1260H 'Chinese military companies' list, which added Alibaba, BYD, Baidu, NIO, CALB Group and Unitree Robotics earlier this month.
MP Materials operates the only active rare earth mine in the US (Mountain Pass, California); USA Rare Earth is the other anchor of Washington's domestic rare earth push.
Han Shen Lin of The Asia Group told CNBC the action is 'largely symbolic' since most listed firms do little China business; the 1260H procurement ban takes effect on June 30.
US-funded enterprises operating inside China are exempted from the procurement ban; companies may apply for licences for goods 'genuinely necessary'.

stories.headline: SoftBank-backed Coowa preps Hong Kong IPO at $3B+ valuation after $600M robotics round

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based Coowa raised more than US$600 million in its latest funding round and is now valued at over US$3 billion.
Coowa plans to file its IPO application in Hong Kong within the next two to three months, with Huatai Securities and Deutsche Bank advising.
The company has deployed more than 10,000 robots across 50+ cities and regions and reported 2025 revenue above 1 billion yuan (~$147.7 million).
Founded in 2015, Coowa began with autonomous-driving technology before moving into physical AI; backers include SoftBank Group and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

stories.headline: Defense tech startups have raised $12.3B in 2026 already, surpassing all of 2025 — Anduril took half

key_facts.fact: Defense technology startups worldwide raised $12.3 billion from venture capital so far in 2026, nearly double the same period last year and already past 2025's full-year total of $9.95 billion, per PitchBook data cited by the Financial Times.
US startups captured $11.4 billion of the $12.3 billion (93%); nearly half of the global total went to Anduril Industries.
Anduril raised an additional $5 billion last month, nearly doubling its valuation in a year to $61 billion; investors include Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.

Investor interest is shifting from heavy hardware to 'asymmetric' cheap, mass-producible weapons — drones, autonomous surface vessels, battlefield AI — after Ukraine and Middle East conflicts showcased their effectiveness.
Mikolaj Firlej, co-founder of European defense-focused VC Expeditions, says drones may be overcrowded but autonomous maritime systems, military satellites and battlefield AI remain in early growth.

stories.headline: Europe heatwave pushes France to 42°C and UK toward 38°C record as red alerts widen

key_facts.fact: France placed 35 of its 96 mainland departments under the highest 'red' heat alert on Sunday June 21, with the number expected to rise to 49 on Monday; temperatures up to 41°C forecast.
42.2°C was recorded in Pissos, southwest France on Sunday; France banned alcohol in red-alert areas and cancelled outdoor sports as wildfire alerts were issued to emergency services and the military.
UK Met Office issued a four-day amber 'extreme heat' warning through Thursday with forecasts reaching 38°C — just under the all-time June record of 35.6°C set in 1976.
Spain declared its first official heatwave of the year from Sunday through Wednesday with temperatures forecast to hit 44°C in some regions.
Italy expanded 'red flag' heat alerts to eight northern and central cities including Bologna, Florence, Milan and Turin.

WHO Europe says more than 200,000 people across Europe died from heat-related causes over the last four years; an attribution study said human-caused climate change killed about 1,500 people in an early May 2026 heatwave.

stories.headline: FDA approves GSK and Spero's Utebzi as the first oral carbapenem antibiotic for complicated UTIs

key_facts.fact: The US FDA approved Utebzi (tebipenem pivoxil) for complicated urinary tract infections including pyelonephritis in adults with limited or no alternative oral options — the first and only oral carbapenem cleared for this indication.
Approval is based on the global Phase III PIVOT-PO non-inferiority trial that enrolled 1,690 patients, comparing oral tebipenem 600 mg q6h to IV imipenem-cilastatin 500 mg q6h for 7–10 days.
The clearance follows a 2022 FDA rejection of Spero's original ADAPT-PO data and a redesigned pivotal study; Spero restructured significantly after the setback before licensing the asset to GSK.
The new oral option could let selected patients avoid or shorten intravenous antibiotic therapy for resistant UTIs, an outpatient-care shift for hospital-discharged patients.

stories.headline: Getty Images signs multi-year display deal with OpenAI to license images for ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: Getty Images Holdings (NYSE: GETY) announced a multi-year display agreement with OpenAI, putting its licensed image library into ChatGPT search and discovery experiences.
Getty CEO Craig Peters said high-quality licensed visual content makes AI-powered search 'more useful and more trustworthy'.
The agreement covers display and attribution only; OpenAI is not permitted to use the images to train its models.
GETY shares recently traded near $0.61, close to the lower end of their 52-week range of about $0.58 to $3.21, when the deal was announced.

stories.headline: Humble Robotics raises $24M to build cabless driverless freight trucks

key_facts.fact: San Francisco-based Humble Robotics raised $24 million to develop an electric, self-driving cabless freight truck.
The vehicle is designed for a 200-mile range and a 55 mph top speed.
The company is pushing to bring driverless freight trucks onto California roads, drawing pushback from human truck drivers.

stories.headline: Apple supplier Lingyi iTech seeks $1.1B in Hong Kong IPO to fund AI hardware and robotics push

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-listed Apple supplier Lingyi iTech aims to raise about US$1.1 billion in a Hong Kong debut scheduled for June 26.
Proceeds are intended to fund the electronic-parts maker's expansion into AI hardware and robotics.

stories.headline: MiniMax releases M2.1, claiming it tops Claude Sonnet 4.5 on multilingual coding

key_facts.fact: MiniMax released MiniMax-M2.1 on June 22, 2026, an update to its M2 model focused on multilingual programming and complex real-world tasks.
MiniMax says M2.1 delivers a significant leap over M2 on core software-engineering leaderboards and 'outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.5 and closely approaches Claude Opus 4.5' in multilingual scenarios.
The model was evaluated on SWE-bench Verified across a variety of coding agent frameworks, which MiniMax says demonstrate 'exceptional framework generalization and robust stability'.

MiniMax also introduced a new benchmark called VIBE (Visual & Interactive Benchmark for Execution) with five subsets — Web, Simulation, Android, iOS, Backend — using an 'Agent-as-a-Verifier' paradigm; M2.1 scored 88.6 average, with 91.5 on VIBE-Web and 89.7 on VIBE-Android.

stories.headline: Morgan Stanley pitches data-center developers on a new leveraged-loan market

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley, one of the most active banks financing data-center developers, is pitching some of those same clients to use leveraged loans rather than bonds.
Morgan Stanley estimates roughly $15 billion of such data-center leveraged loans will be issued in 2026.

stories.headline: Nadella tells WSJ AI giants must earn 'societal permission' as Microsoft pushes lower-cost models

key_facts.fact: In a Wall Street Journal interview published June 21, 2026, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella directly criticized OpenAI and Anthropic by name as 'emblematic' of an industry structured around a few dominant models.
Nadella said: 'You can't say, hey, all white-collar jobs are gone and this could even be a weapon and we will use all the power to build data centers.'
Microsoft is weighing hosting a version of the low-cost Chinese DeepSeek model, despite Anthropic and OpenAI alleging that DeepSeek distilled their top models.
Microsoft has rolled out a suite of low-cost models and released Copilot Cowork, an autonomous agent that lets users choose between AI models for long-running tasks.
The interview escalates an essay Nadella posted on X on June 14, 2026, titled 'A frontier without an ecosystem is not stable', which Tech Times says reached more than 60 million views.
Nadella told the WSJ: 'No amount of just narrative is going to do it because where we are now, we have to sort of walk the walk... We now have to do the hard work in earning the social permission.'

stories.headline: Samsung deploys ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to Korea staff and global DX division

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced Samsung Electronics is deploying ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to all employees in South Korea and to all workers worldwide in its Device eXperience (DX) division.
OpenAI described the rollout as one of its largest enterprise deployments to date, spanning R&D, manufacturing, marketing and corporate functions.
More than 5 million people use Codex every week, and weekly active Codex users in South Korea have risen nearly 800% since February 1, 2026, per OpenAI.
The rollout reverses a 2023 Samsung company-wide ban on ChatGPT, imposed after employees leaked proprietary source code via the chatbot.
The agreement extends an existing collaboration on AI infrastructure; the two firms signed a letter of intent last October for Samsung to supply advanced memory for OpenAI's next-generation systems.

Samsung's Device Solutions semiconductor division, previously using Anthropic's Claude, opened access to ChatGPT on June 12 as part of an 'AX' AI transformation initiative announced in early June 2026.

stories.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung Electronics as South Korea's most valuable listed company

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares closed up 5.61% on Monday, lifting its market cap to 2,080.37 trillion won (US$1.35 trillion); Samsung Electronics slipped 0.14% to a market value of 2,066.66 trillion won (excluding preferred shares).
It is the first time Samsung has been knocked out of the KOSPI No. 1 spot since the streak began in 2000.
SK Hynix shares have rallied more than 340% in 2026, pushing its market value above both Samsung Electronics and Micron and making it the world's most valuable memory-chip maker.
Samsung said any market-cap calculation should include preferred shares, which would bring its value to about 2,246.4 trillion won at Monday's close.
By 2025 SK Hynix captured 61% of the global HBM market, versus Samsung Electronics' 17% and Micron's 21%.
Intraday, SK Hynix touched a record 2.95 million won (~$1,900) before closing at 2.92 million won.

stories.headline: Tencent tests Xiaowei AI assistant inside WeChat, using WeLM and DeepSeek models

key_facts.fact: Tencent has started testing a new AI assistant for WeChat called Xiaowei, available to a small set of users from June 22, 2026.
Xiaowei primarily runs on Weixin's own large language model WeLM, while routing some queries to DeepSeek, per Tencent's customer service unit.
Users interact with Xiaowei via text or voice; it can adjust settings, send messages, hail rides, order food and generate images by tapping WeChat's mini-app ecosystem.
WeChat (Weixin in China) has roughly 1.4 billion users, and Tencent currently trails ByteDance and Alibaba in user adoption and frontier model development.
Tencent already has a separate WeChat-embedded chatbot called Yuanbao; reporting says Xiaowei has been made the company's highest strategic priority despite high rollout costs.
Tencent reportedly led the recent $7.4B fundraising round into DeepSeek and is said to have proposed taking a 20% stake in the startup.

stories.headline: Japan's Toto to invest $495M in semiconductor materials targeting the 1nm era

key_facts.fact: Toto plans to invest 80 billion yen (about $495 million) over the next five years to expand its semiconductor materials unit.
The investment targets R&D for materials used in next-generation 1nm chip production.
Toto, Japan's largest toilet maker, is leveraging its ceramics expertise to expand deeper into the chip-tools supply chain.

stories.headline: Iran reshuts Strait of Hormuz as Vance opens first US–Iran talks under June MoU; Trump threatens fresh strikes

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance led the first US–Iran talks under the June interim peace deal on Sunday at the Qatari-owned Bürgenstock resort in Switzerland, extending the April ceasefire by at least 60 days.
While talks opened, Trump threatened on Truth Social to hit Iran 'very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder' if Tehran did not stop Hezbollah 'proxies' in Lebanon.

Iran announced on Saturday it had again closed the Strait of Hormuz, citing continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon and US 'bad faith'; the previous closure caused 'the biggest disruption of global energy supplies in history'.
A US diplomat told Axios that the parties made 'good progress' on keeping Hormuz open and discussed enforcing the Lebanon ceasefire and the nuclear deal during the talks.
Israel killed at least 29–30 people across southern Lebanon on Saturday, a day after a fresh Israel–Hezbollah ceasefire; total Lebanese death toll since the March 2 offensive exceeds 4,000.
Brent crude opened Monday up more than $1 to $82.30 on the new Hormuz closure, then slid to $79.04 (-1.90%) as Iran said it had secured waivers for oil and petrochemical exports.

stories.headline: WiseTech shares plunge 18% after report Australian Federal Police probe founder Richard White over trafficking and visa-fraud claims

key_facts.fact: WiseTech Global shares fell 18.4% on Monday to A$30.08, the lowest closing level since early June 2021, after reports the Australian Federal Police is investigating executive chairman Richard White.

The AFP's human exploitation taskforce is examining allegations that White exploited a woman's immigration status for sex and provided false information on a visa application, the Australian Financial Review reported.

The complaint to the AFP came from Kathy Phelan, former CEO of Kyckr, a separate White-controlled company, and alleges White made up a reason to hire a woman once employed as a cleaner at WiseTech and supplied false visa information.
The selloff wiped about A$1.8 billion from WiseTech's market value on the day; the stock is down ~75% from its July 2025 peak around A$121.
White stepped down as CEO in late 2024 after a string of personal-life controversies, then returned as executive chairman in February 2026 after a boardroom cleanout.
The same woman, described as Brazilian and identified as Caroline Heidemann, previously made similar allegations and reached a private settlement with White, according to Sky News.
